content:
marco: Quick follow-up on the QKV unification shim we put behind the feature flag in canary yesterday. noticed a small tail latency bump on 2048-step generation for some opt-family models. can we triage?

aisha: saw that in the nightly evals too. p50 unchanged, p95 +12ms, p99 +40-60ms depending on sequence shape. only shows up when rope+bias paths are both enabled.

ben: can you paste the canary config? i want to check kernel selection logs and which fallback path triggered.

marco: config snippet we used: 
```
runtime.features: {
  fused_qkv: on,
  fused_bias_rope: auto,
  dropout_free_infer: on,
  qkv_unify_shim: canary-2024-03
}
routing.policy: prefer_fastpath
```

sophia: thanks. i replayed a few requests and noticed that for odd token lengths the fused kernel rejects due to alignment checks, then we fallback to the fallback path which copies buffers. that's where the 40-60ms shows up.

marco: ok so it's not a math regress, it's an alignment/copying penalty. any quick wins?

ben: two paths: 1) adjust kernel handshake to accept unaligned strides (risky, needs perf test) 2) update shim to pre-pad the kv buffer to aligned size and expose that as a fallback that avoids copy. option 2 seems lower risk.

aisha: option 2 would add a small p50 memory/copy overhead for some requests but would reduce tail. we should quantify memory delta.

telemetry-bot: nightly-eval report: fused-qkv-canary-2024-03: p50=12ms (no change), p95=78ms (+12ms), p99=210ms (+55ms). regression surfaces primarily on model variants: opt-2.7b, llama-13b-instruct.

marco: can we get a tiny repro script? sophia?

sophia: pasted minimal repro (python-ish):
```py
# reproduce alignment fallback
from runtime.client import InferClient
c = InferClient(feature_flags=['qkv_unify_shim'])
input = 'A'*1600  # odd length causing kv packing path A
res = c.generate(input, max_tokens=2048, model='opt-2.7b')
# capture runtime selection logs via RUNTIME_DEBUG=1
```

ben: thanks. i'll add a repeatable kernel selection trace that outputs: model, seq_len, head_size, chosen_kernel, fallback_reason. run it across our canary pool.

marco: proposed plan:
- ben: run kernel-selection trace across 24h of canary traffic, collect shape distribution and fallback reasons
- sophia: prototype pre-pad fallback in shim that pads kv to 256B alignment before calling fused kernel; measure overhead locally
- aisha: run evals with shim-pad enabled to check quality/regressions and memory profile
- if pad reduces tail but keeps cost acceptable, merge behind opt-in flag and roll canary again with metrics gating (p99, cost delta)

sophia: local numbers for pad-fallback prototype: p99 dropped from 210ms->165ms on opt-2.7b replay, memory +2.1% during regen peaks. needs wider verification.

aisha: acceptability thresholds? p99 <= +10ms vs baseline, and cost delta < +3% for canary cohort.

ben: one more ask: expose a lightweight telemetry counter for "fallback_pad_used" in the server logs so we can count how often pad fallback triggers in production. will add to the patch.

marco: good. add rollout guard: if fallback_pad_used > 2% of requests and p99 improvement < 5% then rollback. otherwise proceed to staged rollout.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for runtime-base@canary-shim-pad with changelist CL-4521 by ben. ETA 15m.

marco: if we see any correctness diffs, revert immediately. also please capture per-model histograms so we can tune which models enable pad by default.

aisha: i'll add an evaluation harness to run prompt sets across model variants and diff logits+tokens for regression detection. target run after canary completes.

sophia: leaving a note: long-term we should consider relaxing the fused kernel alignment requirements and add microbenchmarks per head_size/stride so kernel can advertise supported shapes instead of silently rejecting them. that's a follow-up RFC.

marco: agree — put RFC on my plate after this stabilizes. for now we move with pad-shim canary. thanks all :thumbsup:
